title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and historic practices that define the Brooklyn College experience, from the iconic Lily Pond to the legacy of the Brooklyn Bridges.

cards.title: The Lily Pond Graduation Portraits
cards.subtitle: A rite of passage for every graduating senior
cards.notes: Visit the Lily Pond on the East Quad to snap your official graduation photos; it is the most iconic backdrop for BC seniors.
cards.short_summary: The Lily Pond is the central aesthetic landmark of the campus and the primary site for graduation photography.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lily Pond is described as a signature campus feature where students like Nariba Cintron are pictured, and it is a 'happy place' for alumni.
cards.access_notes: Open to students and the public during campus hours; located on the East Quad.

cards.title: The Buster Face Reveal
cards.subtitle: Commencement's high-energy mascot tradition
cards.notes: Watch the 'Buster the Bulldog Face Reveal' video during the commencement ceremony to kick off the graduation festivities.
cards.short_summary: Buster the Bulldog is the official mascot, and his presence is a staple of major campus events and graduation ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: The 101st Commencement Ceremony featured a 'Buster the Bulldog Face Reveal Video' as part of the official program.
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the spring commencement ceremony.

cards.title: The Unspoken Booth Tradition
cards.subtitle: A daily social anchor in the basement of Boylan
cards.notes: Meet friends at a cafeteria booth in Boylan Hall; it's a long-standing 'unspoken tradition' for commuters to gather here.
cards.short_summary: The Boylan Hall cafeteria serves as the primary social hub for the commuter-heavy student body to connect between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Students describe meeting at a booth in the cafeteria as an 'unspoken tradition' and a vital space for socialization.
cards.source_title: Opinion: Where's The Coffee?!? - The Brooklyn College Vanguard
cards.access_notes: Located in the basement of Boylan Hall; open Monday-Thursday 8 AM-7 PM.

cards.title: The 'Brooklyn Bridges' Identity
cards.subtitle: Honoring the former unique mascot
cards.notes: Look for vintage 'Brooklyn Bridges' gear in the archives; the school was the only one in the nation with a bridge mascot until 2010.
cards.short_summary: Before becoming the Bulldogs, Brooklyn College teams were known as the Bridges, a unique nod to the borough's architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: From the mid-nineties to 2010, the mascot was the Brooklyn Bridge, and the teams were called the Brooklyn Bridges.
cards.source_title: Opinion: Bring Back The Brooklyn Bridges
cards.access_notes: Historical mascot; memorabilia can be found in the Brooklyn College Archives.

cards.title: The Historic Country Fair
cards.subtitle: A legacy of campus-wide celebration
cards.notes: Learn about the Country Fair tradition started by Dean Bildersee, which evolved from the college's early 'Field Day' celebrations.
cards.short_summary: The Country Fair was a major historical tradition at Brooklyn College, serving as a primary social event for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Dean Bildersee began the tradition of Country Fair, which followed the earlier 'Field Day' birthday celebrations.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; details preserved in the Brooklyn College Archives.

cards.title: The Alumni Oral History Project
cards.subtitle: Preserving the 'Brooklyn College Story'
cards.notes: Contribute your memories to the Oral History Project to ensure your student experience becomes a permanent part of the college archives.
cards.short_summary: The college actively collects personal stories from alumni to preserve the cultural history of the institution.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brooklyn College Alumni Oral History Project invites alumni to share their stories to preserve memories and accomplishments.
cards.source_title: Alumni Oral History Publication | Brooklyn College
cards.access_notes: Managed by the Office of Alumni Engagement.

cards.title: The Clock Tower Landmark
cards.subtitle: The campus's Georgian-style focal point
cards.notes: Look up at the LaGuardia Library clock tower, the signature building of the campus and a landmark for the Midwood community.
cards.short_summary: The clock tower on LaGuardia Hall is the architectural heart of the campus and its most recognizable symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: The library and its magnificent clock tower became the signature building of the Georgian-style campus.
cards.source_title: The Brooklyn College Library: The Heart of the Academy
cards.access_notes: Visible from the East Quad; library access requires a CUNY ID.

cards.title: The Annual FallFest
cards.subtitle: A signature student life event
cards.notes: Attend FallFest to experience one of the SAIL Center's signature programs designed to build campus pride and community.
cards.short_summary: FallFest is a major recurring event that brings the student body together for social and cultural activities.
cards.evidence_claim: FallFest is listed as a 'Signature Program' by the Student Activities, Involvement, and Leadership (SAIL) Center.
cards.source_title: Student Activities, Involvement, and Leadership (SAIL) - Brooklyn College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; open to all current students.

cards.title: Homecoming at Midwood Field
cards.subtitle: A shared community sports tradition
cards.notes: Head to Midwood Field for the Homecoming game to see the cheer team and band perform in a display of school spirit.
cards.short_summary: Midwood Field is the site for major athletic traditions, including the annual Homecoming festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: Homecoming games at Midwood Field feature performances by the cheer team, band, and step team.
cards.source_title: Hornets Find Their Footing in Homecoming Victory
cards.access_notes: Located just north of the main campus; events are typically seasonal.

cards.title: Bulldogs United Retreat
cards.subtitle: Building leadership and unity
cards.notes: Apply for the Bulldogs United Student Retreat to participate in a signature program focused on personal development and campus unity.
cards.short_summary: This retreat is a key tradition for student leaders to foster inclusivity and strengthen the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bulldogs United Student Retreat is a signature program offered by the SAIL Center to enhance student development.
cards.source_title: Student Activities, Involvement, and Leadership (SAIL) - Brooklyn College
cards.access_notes: Requires application through the SAIL Center; typically held annually.
